subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that Tan⁻¹(1/2) + Tan⁻¹(1/5) + Tan⁻¹(1/8) = π/4.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.73 — SAQ chapter 12 Inverse Trig Functions, answer 76.1, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: TS 18 · AP 15,17,19,20 — five printed tags, the most-asked question in this unit. THREE terms, so the addition formula is applied TWICE — combine two, then combine the result with the third. There is no three-term formula to reach for. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Combine the first two
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. State the formula before using it. Tan⁻¹x + Tan⁻¹y = Tan⁻¹((x+y)/(1−xy)) — both the numerator and the denominator land over 10, and the 10s cancel.

recall.must_convey: That the Tan⁻¹ addition formula is stated and applied to the first two terms, giving Tan⁻¹(7/9).
accept: state the tan inverse addition formula then combine the first two to get tan inverse seven ninths
apply the formula to one half and one fifth giving seven over nine
combine two of the three terms first
modati rendu ni formula tho kalipithe tan inverse seven by nine vasthundi
use tan inverse x plus tan inverse y formula

steps.why: The formula takes exactly two terms. With three, it has to be applied twice — and choosing which two to combine first only affects the arithmetic, not the answer.
common_mistakes: Adding all three arguments at once.

steps.label: Combine with the third
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Same formula again, now with 7/9 and 1/8. Both parts land over 72, and 65/72 over 65/72 is exactly 1.

recall.must_convey: That the formula is applied a second time to Tan⁻¹(7/9) + Tan⁻¹(1/8), giving Tan⁻¹(1).
accept: apply the formula again with seven ninths and one eighth to get tan inverse one
the second application gives sixty five over seventy two over itself which is one
combine the result with the third term
malli formula apply cheste tan inverse one vasthundi
the numerator and denominator are equal so it is tan inverse of one

steps.why: Numerator and denominator coming out identical is the signal that the answer will be Tan⁻¹(1) — a standard angle rather than an awkward one.
common_mistakes: Cancelling before combining and losing the exact match.
Restarting from the original three terms.

steps.label: Evaluate Tan⁻¹(1)
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Tan⁻¹(1) is π/4, since tan(π/4) = 1. Name the standard value rather than leaving it as an inverse.

accept: tan inverse one is pi by four
since tan pi by four is one the answer is pi by four
the value is pi over four
tan inverse one ante pi by four
the answer is pi by four

steps.why: Tan⁻¹(1) is one of the handful of exact inverse values worth knowing by sight — it appears in almost every question of this family.
